techniques.description: Adversaries probe victim networks across port ranges to detect listening services.

telemetry_rules.evidence: Elevated destination port entropy indicates systematic probing across port spectrum.
Multiple distinct destination ports contacted within short time window.

techniques.description: Adversaries execute scans to identify known vulnerable software versions.

telemetry_rules.evidence: High ratio of SYN attempts to established sessions indicates automated scanning probes.
High fanout ratio demonstrates probing fanout across multiple target hosts.

techniques.description: Adversaries search for active services on hosts to find vulnerable listening endpoints.

telemetry_rules.evidence: High connection arrival rate consistent with systematic network service sweep.
Elevated failed connection ratio reflects attempts against non-listening closed ports.

techniques.description: Adversaries exploit weaknesses in Internet-facing programs to gain initial access.

telemetry_rules.evidence: Substantial inbound payload transferred toward public listening port.
Unexpected connection reset behavior following application-level payload delivery.

techniques.description: Adversaries execute rogue code by exploiting vulnerabilities in target processes.

telemetry_rules.evidence: Network retransmission spikes correlate with target process instability during exploit attempts.
High packet size variance reflects exploit payload staging and shellcode injection.

techniques.description: Adversaries repeatedly test passwords against accounts to gain valid access.

telemetry_rules.evidence: Extreme failed connection ratio signifies repeated rejected authentication requests.
Rapid sequential connection attempts against authentication services.

techniques.description: Adversaries log into adjacent internal hosts using remote protocols like SSH, RDP, or SMB.

telemetry_rules.evidence: Connections spreading across multiple distinct internal destination endpoints.
Dominance of reliable TCP sessions typical of management remote desktop and terminal protocols.

techniques.technique_name: Application Layer Protocol: Web C2 Beaconing
techniques.description: Adversaries communicate with command infrastructure over standard HTTP/HTTPS protocols.

telemetry_rules.evidence: Low inter-arrival time standard deviation reveals persistent periodic beaconing heartbeat.
Web protocol encapsulation over standard TCP session.

techniques.description: Adversaries steal sensitive data by transmitting it over non-standard network channels.

telemetry_rules.evidence: Elevated outbound data transmission rate indicates bulk egress of compressed data.
Severe outbound byte asymmetry (outbound volume heavily outweighs inbound responses).

techniques.description: Adversaries steal data by siphoning it through existing command and control infrastructure.

telemetry_rules.evidence: High cumulative outbound byte count along established command channel.
Long-lived flow duration consistent with streaming bulk exfiltration transfer.

techniques.technique_name: Network Denial of Service: Flood Attack
techniques.description: Adversaries degrade target network availability through high-volume traffic flooding.

telemetry_rules.evidence: Extreme packet transmission rate consistent with volumetric network flood.
High burst coefficient of variation indicates coordinated volumetric pulsing.
